result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the plan is a feature tour, and that this is its main weakness. A does more of what the rubric asks: it names the specific sections to cut or hold in reserve, and its 45-minute plan has time set aside for questions plus a next step with a named person, a date and the signer invited. B is stronger at building a start-to-finish scenario around the client's own situations, but it keeps almost every section and squeezes pricing, Q&A and the next step into the last 7 minutes. Neither answer deals well with what each of the three attendees cares about, or how to tell during the demo whether it's working. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly name the feature tour as the core problem. A gives a stronger end-to-end scenario: a sick call plus emergency calls, carried through routing and texts. B scores higher on cutting sections line by line, on checking that the person who signs is in the room, and on a closing schedule that sets aside time for parked questions and a dated next step with an owner. Neither gives a good way to check during the demo whether it is landing with each attendee.
